selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveller believe was the real purpose of worldly life and the core of human life?
questions.answer: He believed the goal of life in this world and the essence of life are found in faith.

questions.question: Why is faith central to the traveller’s approach?
questions.answer: Because he sees faith as the true purpose and inner reality of life.

questions.question: Why does he connect the Qur'an with the Being he is seeking?
questions.answer: Because it is said to be the speech of that Being.

questions.question: Why did he begin by looking at the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Since he lived in the modern age, he first turned to a work from his own time that explains and defends the Qur'an.

questions.question: Why is the Risale-i Nur useful to someone living in the present age?
questions.answer: It gives explanations and evidences suited to a modern setting while drawing from the Qur'an.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the intellectual content of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It describes it as a set of illuminated insights and sound explanations rooted in the Qur'an.

questions.question: Which two sections of the Risale-i Nur are singled out, and what are they said to do?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter are said to show forty dimensions of the Qur'an’s miraculous character.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the author’s confidence in the Qur'an from the decision to give only a few brief indications here?
questions.answer: It shows strong confidence, since even a small sample is presented as enough to point toward its greatness.

questions.question: What kind of response is ruled out for someone who properly sees those demonstrations?
questions.answer: Dismissive criticism is ruled out; admiration is presented as the natural response.

questions.question: In the opening of the passage, how is the traveller described in terms of his spiritual search?
questions.answer: He is shown as deeply driven, never satisfied with shallow answers, and committed to finding truth.

questions.question: Why does he speak to his heart instead of only to his mind?
questions.answer: Because the matter he is exploring involves spiritual commitment as well as reasoning.

questions.question: What action does he decide to take next in his search?
questions.answer: He decides to examine the Qur'an.

questions.question: What feature of the Qur'an’s public role is mentioned to show its confidence and authority?
questions.answer: It openly challenges those who refuse to accept it in every age.

questions.question: How are the parts of the Risale-i Nur characterized?
questions.answer: They are described as many sections made up of insights and dependable explanations derived from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What is the first resource he consults, and why?
questions.answer: He consults the Risale-i Nur first because he lives in the current age and finds in it reflections of the Qur'an’s miraculousness.

questions.question: What does the continued strength of the Risale-i Nur against opposition imply?
questions.answer: It implies that the power behind it comes from a heavenly source, not merely from human effort.

questions.question: What is significant about the claim that forty aspects of miraculousness are established?
questions.answer: It shows the argument is not based on one point only but on many dimensions of evidence.

questions.question: What does the traveller choose not to do after mentioning those proofs?
questions.answer: He chooses not to repeat the full demonstration and instead gives only a short indication of a few signs of greatness.

questions.question: What does the traveller want to learn from the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He wants to learn what it says as the speech of the One he seeks.

questions.question: What does he identify as the book he now needs to investigate?
questions.answer: He identifies the Qur'an as the book he needs to examine.

questions.question: Before studying its message, what did the traveller think had to be established first?
questions.answer: He thought it first had to be shown that the Qur'an comes from the Creator.

questions.question: What must be proven before its teachings can be fully trusted, according to the traveller?
questions.answer: Its origin from the Creator must be established.

questions.question: How do the named sections of the Risale-i Nur function in the argument?
questions.answer: They serve as concentrated demonstrations of many features of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: How do the Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter strengthen this case?
questions.answer: They reportedly lay out forty lines of evidence for the Qur'an’s miraculous nature in a compelling way.
